failure_reason: Genuine Home-scoped New Arrivals PLP found and confirmed, but its site-reported total (221) counts per-color-variant rows, not distinct products (same documented site-wide quirk as Bestsellers, see notes/191.md), and only the first 30 rows are visible via any access tier - the widget's pagination cursor is ignored server-side by both the SSR page and the Next.js data route (verified identical row order/IDs on a cursor-advanced request). The true distinct-product count beyond the visible 30 rows cannot be verified exactly.
notes: Company is Quince (quince.com), a DTC brand spanning apparel and home; scoped strictly to the Home department per task instructions. Checked: homepage nav/mega-menu, /shop/home department page nav, embedded __NEXT_DATA__ nav tree (mega-menu submenuColumnOne/Zero for every department, which explicitly lists a 'Home' -> slug '/shop/home/new-arrivals' entry under the site's global New Arrivals mega-menu, plus a dedicated 'Home New Arrivals' promo entry), sitemap.xml -> sitemap_us.xml -> sitemap_shop.xml (full list of /shop/home/* URLs, includes /shop/home/new-arrivals). Found genuine Home-scoped New Arrivals PLP at /shop/home/new-arrivals (breadcrumb: home > new arrivals; TITLE widget text 'Home New Arrivals'; FILTER_AND_SORT + PRODUCT_LIST widgets present with real product cards, colors/sizes/price filters, sortable by Newest First). This is distinct from /shop/all/new-arrivals (storewide, includes apparel/jewelry/beauty - out of scope) and from per-department pages like /shop/women/new-arrivals, /shop/men/new-arrivals found in nav but not relevant. No further genuine site-exposed sub-splits exist under Home New Arrivals (no 'Furniture New Arrivals'/'Lighting New Arrivals' nav children) - only one undifferentiated listing, so a single row is correct. Not a marketing/editorial 'New Collection' page - it is a real filterable/sortable PLP of newly added Home products, so no ambiguity flag needed on the concept itself. QTY: FILTER_AND_SORT widget reports total=221 and pagination.total=221, but per this site's documented count-inflation pattern (verified in prior Home-Decor pass, notes/191.md), the raw total counts one row per product-color variant, not one row per distinct product. Parsed the full PRODUCT_LIST widget JSON: among the 30 visible rows, only 20 distinct productId values appear. pagination.hasMore=true (221 total rows exist server-side, only 30 delivered in SSR payload). Tried to retrieve further rows: (1) direct GET with cursor=30 on the same URL - server returned page 1 identically; (2) the Next.js data route /_next/data/34214719982/shop/home/new-arrivals.json?cursor=30 - returned byte-identical widget data (same first-5 productIds: 5911,5911,5911,7388,7388) confirming the cursor is ignored server-side; api.onequince.com (client-side incremental loader) has no discoverable public unauthenticated route. Per THE ONE RULE, qty is set to null rather than reporting the inflated 221 or an unverifiable estimate.
